question: If \(x\ge0,\) then \(\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\sqrt{x}}}=\)
solution:
Work from the innermost square root outward. For \(x>0\), taking a square root halves an exponent, while multiplying powers of \(x\) adds their exponents. Thus the middle radical is
\[
\sqrt{x\sqrt{x}}=(x\cdot x^{1/2})^{1/2}=x^{3/4}.
\]
The full expression is therefore
\[
\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\sqrt{x}}}
=(x\cdot x^{3/4})^{1/2}
=x^{7/8}
=\sqrt[8]{x^7}.
\]
When \(x=0\), the original expression and \(\sqrt[8]{x^7}\) both equal \(0\). Hence the answer for every \(x\geq0\) is \(\boxed{\sqrt[8]{x^7}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
